Nah, that's an insane take. No way should a team (that's better before an injury) be counted differently than the same team after an injury. Absolutely insane.

First, do we even understand how many players are out for injuries week in and week out? Across all college football? And you think ANYONE is going to judge a team completely different if they lose a future 1st round offensive lineman out for a game? Hell, no.

Secondly if the entire team the rest of the season is a "shell of itself" because ONE GUY is out, you didn't have a good team, you had a crutch. If you go from an 11-1 team to a 5-7 team because of one guy.... The team is cooked. That means there's NO DEPTH, lack of coaching, no team synergy, on and on.

Lastly, if we're accepting that we're judging performance based off of PERCEIVED individual talent, then how the hell are we saying we're not factoring "power rankings" in to this? Because the guy who plays 3-4 games a season sure as hell doesn't have the actual resume to show they're for real - that somehow they're unlike any other star athlete across any other programs that have had time to watch tape and and game plan around them.

The only fair way I see to rate these games is to look at ACTUAL resume. Tough luck that you might have had a little tougher of a game against an opponent compared to someone else, but that's football. That team lacked depth most of all, but also coaching to make things work after an injury.
